ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a larger circle with O as the center, and coordinate axes are drawn; O is located at the origin. The figure marks P(-1,1), Q(1,1), R(-1,-1), S(1,-1), and all these points are on the large circle. Above there is a semicircle POQ with PQ as diameter and passing through O; below there is a semicircle ROS with RS as diameter and passing through O. Reasoning: From the coordinates, it can be known that PQ is a horizontal line segment, with length 1 - (-1) = 2, so the radius of semicircle POQ is 1, and the area is (1/2)π(1)^2 = π/2. Similarly, the length of RS is also 2, so the radius of semicircle ROS is 1, and the area is also π/2. The sum of the areas of the two semicircles is π. The radius of large circle O is equal to the distance from O to P, namely sqrt((-1)^2 + 1^2) = sqrt(2), therefore the area of the large circle is π(sqrt(2))^2 = 2π. So the required ratio is π / 2π = 1/2.

raw_record.question_text: Semicircles $POQ$ and $ROS$ pass through the center of circle $O$. What is the ratio of the combined areas of the two semicircles to the area of circle $O$?

method.method_draft: Use the coordinate labels shown in the diagram. Read that the large circle is centered at O=(0,0) and contains points P(-1,1), Q(1,1), R(-1,-1), and S(1,-1). For the upper semicircle POQ, the endpoints P and Q lie on the horizontal segment y=1, so its diameter is PQ=2 and its radius is 1; the drawn arc passes through O, matching the lower half of the circle centered at (0,1). Similarly, the lower semicircle ROS has diameter RS=2 and radius 1. Each semicircle has area (1/2)π(1)^2, so together they have area π. The radius of circle O is the distance from O to P, Q, R, or S: sqrt(1^2+1^2)=sqrt(2), so its area is π(sqrt(2))^2=2π. The desired ratio is π/(2π)=1/2.
